HTPN LEGACY
WHY THIS CONVENTION

MORE THAN A CONVENTION.
MALAYSIA'S LIGHTHOUSE
HOSPITAL IN ACTION.

HTPN's Healthcare Intelligence Office has built over 50 live clinical applications entirely in-house — without external vendors, without high-cost licences. Led by practicing clinicians, the HIO has transformed how a 137-year-old public hospital builds digital solutions.

This convention shares that model — openly, freely — with every KKM hospital in Malaysia. Come to learn, compete, and take the insourcing revolution home.

  • Insourcing model — built by clinicians, for clinicians
  • Free entry for all KKM staff & healthcare professionals
  • National-level recognition through MPC case study documentation
  • Reward culture — celebrate innovation on a national stage
FEATURED SPEAKERS

LEARN FROM THOSE

HEALTHCARE AI FUTURE

From AI ethics pioneers to hardware deployment experts to reward culture champions — Innova-thon brings UPM and UiTM's leading researchers to the national stage. Expect practical insights, clinical depth, and talks that move beyond theory.

MARKING RUBRIC

Every project is evaluated against eight standardised criteria.

01—  Clear Problem Statement Addresses a real clinical or operational gap with a well-defined, justified solution.
02—  Creativity Original idea that stands apart from existing solutions in the field.
03—  User Friendly Intuitive interface adoptable by end-users without complex training.
04—  Deployment Technically stable and integrates with existing hospital systems.
05—  Data Validation AI model is accurate, data-secure, and privacy-compliant.
06—  Clear Output & Outcome Delivers measurable results — time saved, accuracy gained, costs reduced.
07—  Scalability Can be adopted beyond the originating hospital or team.
08—  Sustainability Cost-effective and operable without reliance on external vendors.

IMPORTANT INFO

  • No registration fees required.
  • Travel claims are the responsibility of your own department (PTJ masing-masing).
  • 1 project = 1 presenter only on Innovathon Day.
  • Pre-Workshop registration automatically registers you for Innovathon Day.
  • In-house development only – no vendor-assisted or black-box algorithms.
  • Data must be synthetic/dummy only/anonymised/de-identified.

PATIENT DATA RESTRICTIONS

Real patient data is STRICTLY PROHIBITED unless you have:

  1. Explicit written approval from your Hospital Director
  2. Registered (NMRR) and Ethical Clearance (MREC)
  3. Compliance to PDPA

09:30 AM PLENARY 1Prof. Madya Dr Mohd Rafee bin BaharudinAI Transformation in Healthcare: Roadmap, Strategy & Vision – 2030 Prediction ▼
AI Transformation in Healthcare: Roadmap, Strategy & Vision – 2030 Prediction

An authoritative overview of the current AI landscape across Malaysia's public health ecosystem — from clinical decision support to population health analytics. Prof Rafee draws on his WHO-funded research to map where AI is already reshaping patient outcomes, where the critical gaps remain, and what ethical and data governance frameworks must underpin every deployment. A roadmap for what Malaysia's healthcare future can and must look like.

Faculty of Medicine & Health Sciences · Universiti Putra Malaysia
10:00 AM PLENARY 2Prof. Madya Dr Shukor SanimGrant Opportunities, Networking & Potential University Collaboration in AI Healthcare ▼
Grant Opportunities, Networking & Potential University Collaboration in AI Healthcare

A practical masterclass in navigating Malaysia's research funding landscape for AI-driven healthcare projects. Prof Shukor demystifies the grant application process — from Ministry of Higher Education funding to international research collaborations — and reveals what review panels are really looking for. He also covers hardware investment realities (GPU infrastructure, cloud vs on-premise), AI tool selection frameworks, and how clinical teams can position their work for academic co-authorship and sustained institutional support.

Faculty of Computer & Mathematical Sciences · UiTM Perlis
10:30 AM PLENARY 3Dr Ahmad Hakiim JamaluddinAI Transformation of Reward Culture & Quick-Win Projects ▼
AI Transformation of Reward Culture & Quick-Win Projects – Experience in Participating and Organising International AI Competitions

Why do some hospital teams build extraordinary AI solutions while others stall? Dr Hakiim presents a compelling evidence-based framework for engineering an innovation culture from the ground up — using structured reward systems, well-designed AI competitions, and recognition pathways that make clinicians feel their contributions matter at a national level. Drawing from his experience running large-scale AI challenges, he covers competition design, rubric construction, AI model evaluation methodology, and how to sustain innovation momentum long after the competition ends.

Department of Mathematics & Statistics · Universiti Putra Malaysia
11:00 AM PLENARY 4Ts. Mohd Azirudin bin SahhudinFrom Idea to Ownership: Copyrighting Your Innovations ▼
From Idea to Ownership: Copyrighting Your Innovations

Your team built it — now protect it. A practical guide to intellectual property for clinician-innovators: what can and cannot be copyrighted, how to register your software and digital solutions in Malaysia, and how ownership works when innovations are built inside a public hospital. Walk away knowing exactly how to turn your in-house application into a protected, citable asset.

Politeknik Port Dickson (PoliPD)
11:30 AM Breakout Sessions — AM Session (Innova-thon Competition) ▼

Parallel breakout sessions running simultaneously · 8 min presentation + 4 min Q&A per project

Key Updates
Judging Categories
Projects are judged in the three original categories: Patient Journey, Clinician Journey, and Management Productivity.
Breakout Rooms
There will be exactly 3 breakout rooms, one per category. Proceed directly to your assigned room after the morning plenary.
Judges Allocation
The 13 judges are split across the 3 breakout rooms so each category is assessed by its own panel.
Scoring System
Judging is 100% on the event day, 21 July 2026 — all scoring is done live, replacing the earlier pre-judging plan.
Time Allocation
Strictly 10 min presentation + 5 min Q&A per team.Total: 15 minutes
Find Your Breakout Room

Teams are assigned to one of three breakout rooms by category. After the morning plenary, proceed directly to your assigned room. Tap a room to see its moderator, judges, and team list.

Frequently Asked Questions
Formal or smart casual. The hall can get cold, so bring a suit jacket, blazer, or sweater.
Optional but recommended. If you can bring your own device, great. If not, no problem — we'll open your submitted links on the day (5-slide deck, 3-minute video pitch, and app deployment link). An HDMI cable is provided.

The judging panel requires every 5-slide presentation to cover these seven points:

1
Problem StatementClearly define the issue or challenge your project aims to solve.
2
ObjectiveState the goal(s) of your project.
3
MethodologyExplain the approach, tools, and process used to develop your solution.
4
Productivity: Measurable ImpactA before/after comparison backed by observation, facts, or data — time or cost savings, reduced errors, or shorter complaints/queues.
5
Potential Stakeholders & Value of OutcomesThe value generated if scaled — affecting patients, clinicians, and management; highlight RKB-style gains.
6
Future ImprovementsOutline possible enhancements and next steps.
7
App Deployment LinkA demonstration of live app functionality.
Yes. A buffet is served three times a day at Restoran Lauk Kampung (ground floor). Please enjoy the meals and network. Vegetarian? Please select the vegetarian option.
